root_cause.text: zram_bvec_write_partial() passes the parent bio to zram_read_page(), causing asynchronous backing device reads to be dispatched while the caller immediately frees the buffer, resulting in use-after-free when the async read completes and writes to the freed page.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes the zram_read_page() call from passing `bio` (the parent bio) to passing `NULL`. The CVE description explicitly states that "zram_read_page() picks the sync or async backing device read path based on whether the parent bio is NULL" and that passing the parent bio causes "the read is dispatched asynchronously and zram_read_page() returns 0 while the bio is still in flight." The caller then immediately executes memcpy_from_bvec(), zram_write_page(), and __free_page() on the buffer, leaving "the async read to write into a freed page." The commit message notes this was a missed fix—zram_bvec_read_partial() had already been corrected in commit 4e3c87b9421d for the same reason.

candidates.rationale: This statement passes the parent bio to zram_read_page(), which causes asynchronous backing device reads to be dispatched. Since the caller immediately frees the buffer after this function returns, the async read operation will eventually complete and attempt to write to the already-freed page, resulting in use-after-free. The fix changes this to pass NULL instead of bio to prevent async dispatch in this partial write context.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement passes the parent bio parameter to zram_read_page() within zram_bvec_write_partial(). This causes zram_read_page() to dispatch asynchronous backing device reads using the bio context. However, since zram_bvec_write_partial() returns immediately after this call, the caller frees the buffer. When the async read completes later, it attempts to write to the already-freed page, resulting in use-after-free. The fix changes this to pass NULL instead of bio to prevent async dispatch in this partial write context.

commit 4e3c87b9421df497d849ae61aab9762de7f66afb
Author: Christoph Hellwig <hch@lst.de>
Date:   Tue Apr 11 19:14:58 2023 +0200

    zram: fix synchronous reads
    
    Currently nothing waits for the synchronous reads before accessing the
    data.  Switch them to an on-stack bio and submit_bio_wait to make sure the
    I/O has actually completed when the work item has been flushed.  This also
    removes the call to page_endio that would unlock a page that has never
    been locked.
    
    Dr
bic_trace_step.reason: This commit FIXES the vulnerability rather than introducing it. The root cause was that zram_bvec_write_partial() passed the parent bio to zram_read_page(), which then dispatched asynchronous backing device reads while the caller immediately freed the buffer, causing use-after-free. The fix in this commit changes zram_sync_read() to use an on-stack bio with submit_bio_wait() instead of chaining to the parent bio. Specifically: (1) The zram_sync_read() function now creates a local 'struct bio bio' on the stack and uses 'submit_bio_wait(&bio)' to synchronously wait for completion before returning, eliminating the async completion race. (2) The read_from_bdev_sync() function no longer takes a 'struct bio *bio' parameter - it no longer passes the parent bio. (3) In zram_bvec_read_partial(), the call is changed from 'zram_read_page(zram, page, index, bio, true)' to 'zram_read_page(zram, page, index, NULL)', explicitly passing NULL instead of the parent bio. (4) The zram_page_end_io() callback that was handling async completion is removed entirely. These changes ensure synchronous reads complete before the buffer is freed, preventing the use-after-free vulnerability.
